messages:
customer-ops: @meera heads-up — AcmeHealth says SSO logins started failing right after their IdP rotated signing certs. Users see an immediate error page with 'Invalid SAML Response' and our logs show 'Recipient mismatch' + 'Assertion consumer URL not recognized'.
meera: Can you paste the exact SAML Response (base64) or a SAML trace? Need the <Assertion> attributes and the Recipient/Audience values. Also the IdP metadata URL they used.
customer-ops: I asked them to upload the raw SAMLResponse and they attached it to the ticket (ticket #CE-4129). Link: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/CE-4129 — they've also given the IdP metadata endpoint: https://idp.acmehealth.example/metadata.xml
samira: quick sanity check: did they rotate both signing and encryption certs? Rotation sometimes leaves an old cert in the metadata until it's propagated. If the SP still validates against the old fingerprint it fails.
jonathan: If we see 'Recipient mismatch' usually the Recipient in the Assertion (Assertion/Subject/SubjectConfirmation/Data/@Recipient) doesn't exactly match the AssertionConsumerService URL in our SP metadata. Common gotchas: trailing slash, http vs https, or proxy rewriting (X-Forwarded-Proto).
customer-ops: They confirm ACS URL in IdP is "https://app.redwood.ai/saml/consume" (no trailing slash). Our console shows configured ACS is "https://app.redwood.ai/saml/consume/" (with trailing slash).
meera: That explains Recipient mismatch. Two approaches: 1) Ask IdP to update ACS to exact SP URL (fast), or 2) We can temporarily accept both variants on our SP tunnel for 48h while they fix metadata. I'll coordinate with infra.
infra-ops: We can add a temporary allowed recipient list entry for the customer on the auth proxy. Command to add (run from auth-admin box):
```
# add allowed recipient for tenant acme
redis-cli HSET saml:tenant:acme allowed_recipients 2 "https://app.redwood.ai/saml/consume"
service auth-proxy reload
```
Note: do this only after verifying the base64 SAMLResponse's Recipient value.
jonathan: Also confirm the Assertion Audience (Assertion/Conditions/AudienceRestriction/Audience) matches the SP entityID. If the customer used an old entityID in their metadata the Audience check fails with 'Audience invalid'.
meera: @customer-ops can you request a SAML trace (SAML-tracer plugin or browser devtools) so we can confirm both Recipient and Audience values? Ask them to redact user PII.
customer-ops: Sent the SAMLResponse (base64) into the ticket, plus IdP metadata XML. I dumped the response locally and base64-decoded the Assertion. The Recipient is exactly "https://app.redwood.ai/saml/consume" (no slash). Audience is "urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth-v1" but our current SP entityID is "urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth" — looks like a mismatch.
samira: aha — that Audience mismatch will result in a 'Audience invalid' failure even if Recipient matches. It implies their IdP is still using an older integration config with a different entityID namespace. Two remediation steps: ask IdP to update Audience to match our entityID, or we can add the older entityID as an accepted audience for this tenant.
infra-ops: To add legacy entityID for tenant acme (temporary):
```
# add accepted audiences
redis-cli SADD saml:tenant:acme:accepted_audiences "urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth-v1"
service auth-proxy reload
```
Keep this as a short-lived exception and log it.
meera: Security note: before adding exceptions, confirm cert rotation didn't also change signature algorithms. We had one case where the IdP switched to RSA-PSS and our validator wasn't configured for it. If that's the case we'll need a library bump.
support-bot: [automated] New ticket CE-4129 created and linked. Assigned: meera. Priority: P1 (customer-facing outage).
jonathan: For the cert fingerprint check — ask them to provide the cert in PEM or the metadata xml. We can extract the cert and run:
```
# extract cert from metadata (example)
curl -fsS https://idp.acmehealth.example/metadata.xml | xmllint --xpath 'string(//KeyDescriptor/KeyInfo/X509Data/X509Certificate)' - | sed 's/\n//g' > idp-cert.b64
openssl base64 -d -A -in idp-cert.b64 -out idp-cert.der
openssl x509 -inform der -in idp-cert.der -noout -fingerprint -sha256
```
That gives the SHA256 fingerprint we compare with their cert rotation notes.
customer-ops: They included metadata.xml; I ran the extraction and their cert fingerprint changed at 2026-03-12T21:00Z per their logs. They said they uploaded new metadata to the IdP admin portal, but downstream caches maybe stale (CDN in front of metadata endpoint).
meera: If metadata is cached (either at the IdP or our side) we need to check our metadata refresh interval. Our system refreshes IdP metadata every 6 hours by default; for P1 we can trigger a manual refresh for this tenant:
```
# trigger metadata refresh
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://auth-admin.redwood.ai/admin/tenants/acme/refresh-idp
```
I'll run it once we confirm the exact metadata URL.
jonathan: Also watch the signature validation logs (auth-proxy logs at /var/log/auth-proxy/saml.log). Search for lines with 'Audience check failed' or 'Recipient mismatch' and include the full exception text in the ticket. That speeds root cause.
customer-ops: I've uploaded the saml.log snippet and included the exception: "AudienceRestriction failed: expected urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth but got urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth-v1". They updated IdP to use our entityID and re-tested — they still get failure due to Recipient trailing slash mismatch.
samira: Tell them to update the ACS in IdP to exactly match our console value (or vice versa). If they can't change it quickly, we'll apply the temporary allowed recipient patch and accepted audience patch together, then remove both after they confirm.
meera: I'll coordinate the temporary exceptions: infra, please add the allowed recipient and accepted_audience entries for tenant acme, and then reload auth-proxy. I'll add an audit entry and set a 48-hour TTL to auto-clean.
infra-ops: Done. Added entries and reloaded. Confirmed via logs: "Allowed recipient matched: https://app.redwood.ai/saml/consume" and "Accepted audience matched: urn:redwood:sp:acmehealth-v1".
customer-ops: Customer retested — login succeeded for 4/5 users, one user still hitting an error (browser cached SAML assertion?). They logged out and cleared cache and it worked. All clear on their side.
meera: Great. Action items: 1) customer to update IdP metadata to final values (entityID + ACS) and confirm propagation. 2) we will remove the temporary exceptions in 48h automatically; if they need more time open a follow-up PR. 3) add a short KB article documenting recipient trailing-slash gotcha + quick commands.
jonathan: KB draft — include the openssl fingerprint steps, how to decode SAMLResponse, and sample redis commands (but mark them as infra-only).
support-bot: [automated] CE-4129 status -> resolved (temp workaround applied). Keep ticket open for 48h to confirm permanence. :white_check_mark:
meera: Thanks everyone. I'll paste the final remediation steps into the ticket and notify Acme to update their IdP metadata.
customer-ops: Noting customer thanks: "Thanks Redwood team — appreciate the quick workaround and guidance." :pray:
